pr_title: fix(rust,python): Add ability to read csv columns as `Int8`, `Int16`, `UInt8`, `UInt16`
pr_body:
Fixes #5214 

For some reason, I had to bump `clap` from `3.2.22` to `4.0.18` in order to build; not sure why this is the case but it's included with this PR only because I was forced down this route.
pr_comments: Hm, I seem to have somehow mixed-and matched things while compiling locally and didn't see the errors. Apologies; I'll leave this PR open and fix the mistakes.
I don't want the extra code bloat for this. We need to parse with existing types and downcast later.

As well, not sure if this is a separate issue or a side-effect of the (undesired) implementation so only putting this here as a comment for now. It would seem the dtypes are not maintained anyway, making this a potentially futile exercise. For example:

```python
import io
import polars as pl

data = """a,b,c
1,2,127
,,
3,-9,127"""

f = io.BytesIO()
f.write(data.encode("utf-8"))
f.seek(0)
(
    pl.read_csv(
        f,
        has_header=True,
        dtypes=[pl.UInt8, pl.Int16, pl.Int8],
    )
    .sum()
)
```
gives
```
shape: (1, 3)
┌─────┬─────┬─────┐
│ a   ┆ b   ┆ c   │
│ --- ┆ --- ┆ --- │
│ i64 ┆ i64 ┆ i64 │
╞═════╪═════╪═════╡
│ 4   ┆ -7  ┆ 254 │
└─────┴─────┴─────┘
```
which kind of defeats the purpose I would think.

> I don't want the extra code bloat for this. We need to parse with existing types and downcast later.

Continuing on what I said earlier. We need to downcast later and use the parsers that are already in place. You can use the `to_cast` information for that.

Here is the snippet that prepares `to_cast` https://github.com/pola-rs/polars/blob/33da4a85871216e39f708e7210fc8fea9c674e0f/polars/polars-io/src/csv/read.rs#L367.
@DeliciousHair, I think you are on the right path. I have left a few comments.

@ritchie46 Apologies for leaving this for so long, the 9-5 has been taking up a lot more than that the past few weeks. Trying to fix this up now though and I'm having some problems regarding the ownership of `reader_bytes` that has me just going in circles; hoping there is a more skilled person around that may be able to lend a hand.

Basic version of attempted solution is:

```rust
let reader_bytes = get_reader_bytes(&mut self.reader)?;
...
let (schema, to_cast, _has_cat) = self.prepare_schema_overwrite(&schema);
...
let mut csv_reader = self.core_reader(
    Some(&schema),
    to_cast,
    Some(reader_bytes)
)?;
```

this doesn't work, as expected:
```shell
error[E0502]: cannot borrow `self` as immutable because it is also borrowed as mutable
   --> polars/polars-io/src/csv/read.rs:552:51
    |
528 |                 let reader_bytes = get_reader_bytes(&mut self.reader)?;
    |                                                     ---------------- mutable borrow occurs here
...
552 |                 let (schema, to_cast, _has_cat) = self.prepare_schema_overwrite(&schema);
    |                                                   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ immutable borrow occurs here
...
568 |                     Some(reader_bytes)
    |                          ------------ mutable borrow later used here

error[E0499]: cannot borrow `self` as mutable more than once at a time
   --> polars/polars-io/src/csv/read.rs:565:38
    |
528 |                   let reader_bytes = get_reader_bytes(&mut self.reader)?;
    |                                                       ---------------- first mutable borrow occurs here
...
565 |                   let mut csv_reader = self.core_reader(
    |  ______________________________________^
566 | |                     Some(&schema),
567 | |                     to_cast,
568 | |                     Some(reader_bytes)
    | |                          ------------ first borrow later used here
569 | |                 )?;
    | |_________________^ second mutable borrow occurs here
```

The "obvious" solution (to my amateur thinking anyway) is to deref `reader_bytes`, but that doesn't seem to work. This compiles:
```rust
let reader_bytes = {
    let rb = get_reader_bytes(&mut self.reader)?;
    ReaderBytes::Owned(rb.deref().to_vec())
};
```
but then leads to other problems at run-time of the form:
```shell
Error: InvalidOperation(Owned("Cannot create polars series from Int8 type"))
```

Any pointers? I'm rather stuck.
I am closing this as the PR has not been updated in a while. Also, I believe we have this functionality now in the `dtypes` parameter for `read_csv`.

issue_context.title: pl.read_csv() does not recognize U/Int8, U/Int16 dtypes
issue_context.body:
### Polars version checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Issue description

When providing 1- and 2-byte integer dtypes to `pl.read_csv()`, a `ComputeError` is raised.

### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
from io import BytesIO

for dtype in [pl.UInt8, pl.Int8, pl.UInt16, pl.Int16, pl.UInt32, pl.Int32,  pl.UInt64, pl.Int64]:
    buffer = BytesIO()
    pl.DataFrame({'a': pl.Series([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], dtype=dtype)}).write_csv(buffer)

    try:
        pl.read_csv(buffer, dtypes=[dtype])
    except Exception as e:
        print(e)

    output.close()
```
```
Unsupported data type UInt8 when reading a csv
Unsupported data type Int8 when reading a csv
Unsupported data type UInt16 when reading a csv
Unsupported data type Int16 when reading a csv
```

### Expected behavior

No output

### Installed versions

<details>

```
---Version info---
Polars: 0.14.18
Index type: UInt32
Platform: Windows-10-10.0.19044-SP0
Python: 3.9.5 (tags/v3.9.5:0a7dcbd, May  3 2021, 17:27:52) [MSC v.1928 64 bit (AMD64)]
---Optional dependencies---
pyarrow: 8.0.0
pandas: 1.4.3
numpy: 1.23.1
fsspec: <not installed>
connectorx: 0.3.0
xlsx2csv: 0.8
matplotlib: 3.6.1
```

</details>
comments: Was there an hack to fix the issue in the Python API? It's odd to me that the Python API `read_csv` does support U/Int8 and U/Int16 types now. However, the Rust API `CsvReader::with_dtypes` does NOT support U/Int8, U/Int16 types.
Did you activate the dtype features?

@ritchie46,

You were right! Including the `dtype-full` feature made it work.

While `read_csv` now supports reading 1 & 2-byte integers, both `read_csv_batched` and `scan_csv` report that it is not supported: `Unsupported data type Int8 when reading a csv`
Scanning as 4-byte integers and downcasting before a `collect()` uses significantly more memory (e.g. for large arrays of genoytpes). Workaround for now is to use `read_csv_batched` in smaller chunks.

> While `read_csv` now supports reading 1 & 2-byte integers, both `read_csv_batched` and `scan_csv` report that it is not supported: `Unsupported data type Int8 when reading a csv` Scanning as 4-byte integers and downcasting before a `collect()` uses significantly more memory (e.g. for large arrays of genoytpes). Workaround for now is to use `read_csv_batched` in smaller chunks.

The problem is that `LazyCsvReader::with_dtype_overwrite` does not support these datatypes, while `CsvReader::with_dtypes` does.

review_comments: Why do these need to be cast? We have have native support for these.

I may have altered something via the match arms, but what seems to be happening is that if either of `self.schema_overwrite` or `self.dtype_overwrite` are set, then `self.prepare_schema_overwrite(schema)` is used which, in turn, uses the casting. Without this (superfluous) cast in here, I couldn't seem to get the buffer to read the dtype as specified. I'll look again though.

This means we call this one twice on a csv read. This can be a full disk read in the case of compressed csv's so if we call this we should keep the reader_bytes and initialize the core reader with it.

Yup, and I agree that this is far from a decent approach. I did not want to get too into the weeds with the whole header-parsing logic though as that seemed well beyond my current skill level in terms of code I would be touching for this small problem. I would very much welcome some suggestions regarding how to actually remove this (silly) two-step solution.

I think we should could add an `optional` reader_bytes argument to the core reader.

Then you pass the reader_bytes you just created and then let the core reader continue doing its work.
Can you remove these changes from git? I would not expect any changes in `buffer.rs` for this fix.
